name: Unowned Collective // Body Autonomy Runner Vest
description:
A tactical mesh vest produced in rotating underground print runs by the Unowned Collective — a loose network of synthetic-rights activists and anti-corponation runners. Front panel displays a bold stencil print: 'NO SERIAL. NO OWNER. NO CORP.' in Hausa-Portuguese pidgin and Standard Meridian glyphs. Back panel varies by print run — current edition shows a cracked corporate ownership barcode over a synthetic's exposed chassis art.

Construction is deliberately utilitarian: MOLLE-compatible webbing, reflective piping on side seams, a chest channel for runner cable management. The vest is designed to be worn visibly, loudly, in contested spaces. Wearing one in Tier 4 or above is considered a provocation. Synthetics who wear it are making a specific legal and philosophical statement.
functionality: MOLLE webbing accepts standard pouches and tool attachments. Reflective piping improves low-light visibility for runners. Cable management channel routes BCI or comm lines cleanly from collar to waist. Lightweight and breathable for active wear.
what_it_says: I am not property, I am not compliant, and I want every camera to see me say it.
manufacturer: Unowned Collective (underground rotating print, no fixed address)
story_hooks: A new print run contains a hidden steganographic message in the barcode art — someone is using the vests as a dead-drop communication system.
Corporate security has started arresting vest-wearers in Tier 4 zones under a new 'incitement of synthetic unrest' statute; the Collective needs a lawyer and a loud response.
A Tier 5 exec's synthetic personal assistant shows up to a board meeting wearing one — and refuses to remove it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately confrontational tactical mesh vest with bold political messaging. Sleeveless, modular, built for visibility in urban resistance spaces. The front declares defiance in multiple languages; the back features anti-corporate imagery. Worn by runners, activists, and liberated synthetics as a statement garment.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, oversized utility fit designed to layer over augmentation rigs and under armor. Sits at mid-hip with generous armholes for mobility and cable routing. Built for function over form, with intentional room for tech integration.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty ballistic mesh weave with synthetic-polymer reinforcement. MOLLE webbing panels rated for modular attachment. Reflective piping threaded with light-reactive filament.
physical_description.texture: Open mesh with visible grid pattern, tactile webbing straps, raw seams deliberately left exposed. High contrast between soft mesh and rigid attachment points. Stencil print creates raised texture on front panel.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray base mesh with high-contrast white stenciled text ('NO SERIAL. NO OWNER. NO CORP.'). Back panel: cracked red barcode graphic on black, mimicking corrupted corporate ownership tags. Neon-white reflective piping on side seams.
physical_description.closures: Side-seam friction-fit with industrial velcro strips and magnetic snap closures at shoulders. Chest channel uses tension clips for cable management—no exposed zippers.
distinctive_features: Front stencil text in Hausa-Portuguese pidgin and Standard Meridian glyphs
Back panel with cracked barcode and synthetic liberation artwork
MOLLE-compatible webbing for modular gear attachment
Integrated chest cable channel for runner tech and neural interfaces
Reflective side piping with embedded light-reactive threads
Deliberately raw seams and visible stitching as design statement
Variable back panel art per rotating print run
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 / Counter-cultural. Officially illegal in Tier 1-2 corporate enclaves. Worn as explicit provocation against ownership structures.
physical_description.cultural_context: Unowned Collective activist and liberation runner wear. Signals opposition to corporate personhood claims, synth-rights advocacy, and anti-augmentation gatekeeping. Wearing one in policed zones risks detainment. A defiant statement of body autonomy.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually broken-in with visible wear—scuffed reflective piping, faded stencil print from exposure, stress fractures around velcro attachment points. Worn gear is worn loudly; pristine vests suggest recent recruitment.
